newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberia confirms fuel surcharge on cargo.
newsitem.headline: Iberia confirms fuel surcharge on cargo.

text.p: Iberia has introduced a surcharge of 13 pesetas (10 cents) a kilo on international cargo from November 5, an Iberian cargo official told Reuters.
Earlier on Thursday cargo industry sources in Madrid said Iberia had introduced this surcharge from November 11.
Domestic cargo rates, which were increased only in May, are not affected and large cargoes contracted recently at a specially negotiated price are also excluded.

"Iberia had been talking of raising cargo prices on January 1 next year, but fuel prices have continued to climb and other airlines had already made the move," the official said. "It's simply bringing forward a planned rise."
Lufthansa, British Airways, Air France, KLM and Swissair have already announced a fuel surcharge on cargo and in some cases passenger fares.
Iberia said passenger fares would not be affected, but the company had delayed further planned cuts in fares because of the higher fuel prices.
The 13 peseta surcharge applies to Spanish origin cargo. There are variations on cargo originating on other countries because of exchange rate differences.
The surcharge is likely to be removed if and when oil prices retreat from their recent highs, the official added.

The airline released figures earlier Thursday showing cargo business was particularly strong in October, the beginning of the peak season, and that it had flown 594 million freight tonne kms in the first 10 months of this year, up nine percent from the same period 1995.
In 1995 as a whole it flew 724 million freight tonne kms and earned 30.8 billion pesetas from its cargo business. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
